title: Household Loans, August 2025
content: In August 2025, household loan balances rose by KRW4.7 trillion, up KRW2.3 trillion from July, while other loan types fell by KRW0.4 trillion, down KRW1.9 trillion. In the banking sector, household loans increased by KRW4.2 trillion (up KRW2.8 trillion), with mortgage loans rising from KRW2.2 trillion to KRW2.7 trillion and policy‑based loans steady at KRW1.2 trillion. Other banking loans fell from KRW0.6 trillion to KRW0.3 trillion. In the non‑banking sector, household loans grew KRW0.6 trillion, reversing a KRW0.5 trillion decline. Mutual finance growth accelerated from KRW0.4 trillion to KRW1.2 trillion; savings banks moved from a KRW0.3 trillion decline to a KRW0.03 trillion rise; insurance and specialized credit firms saw flat declines of KRW0.4 trillion and KRW0.2 trillion respectively. Compared with the same month a year earlier, the August rise of KRW4.7 trillion is slower than the KRW9.7 trillion increase seen in August 2024, but faster than the previous month’s KRW2.3 trillion gain. Seasonal factors such as a surge in mortgage demand (KRW4.2 trillion to KRW5.1 trillion) and increased housing transactions explain much of the growth. Authorities note concerns over potential interest‑rate cuts and rising housing prices, and will continue monitoring and enforcing strengthened housing‑loan regulations, including on‑site inspections and regular meetings with financial firms.

title: 兴业银行：上半年实现归母净利润431.41亿元，同比增长0.21%_银行_金融频道首页_财经网 - CAIJING.COM.CN
content:
Industrial Bank released its 2025 first‑half financial report on 28 August 2025. The bank reported operating revenue of 1104.58 billion yuan, a 2.29% decline year‑over‑year, with the decline narrowing by 1.29 percentage points compared to the first quarter. Net profit attributable to parent‑company shareholders rose to 431.41 billion yuan, a 0.21% increase year‑over‑year, turning the growth rate from negative in the first quarter to positive. Interest net income fell 1.52% to 737.55 billion yuan, largely due to a tighter interest‑rate spread; the net interest margin was 1.75%, down 7 basis points from the previous year.

Total assets reached 10.61 trillion yuan at the end of the first half, up 1.01% from the end of last year. Loans to customers stood at 5.90 trillion yuan, a 2.91% increase. Green loans grew 15.61%, technology loans 14.73%, and medium‑term manufacturing loans 11.83%, all outpacing overall loan growth. Deposits were 5.87 trillion yuan, up 6.10%; the deposit interest rate was 1.76%, down 22 basis points from the previous year, while the interbank deposit rate also fell to 1.76%, a 47‑basis‑point decline. The average cost of interest‑bearing liabilities was 1.86%, down 31 basis points.

Asset quality remained stable. Non‑performing loan (NPL) balance was 634.93 billion yuan, up 20.16 billion yuan from the end of last year, giving an NPL ratio of 1.08%—unchanged from the first quarter and 0.01 percentage points higher than the previous year. The NPL coverage ratio was 228.54%, indicating a robust buffer.

title: الصين.. زيادة 46ر13 تريليون يوان في القروض المقومة باليوان خلال 8 شهور
content:
The People's Bank of China released official data showing that yuan‑denominated loans rose by 46.13 trillion yuan (about 9.1 trillion U.S. dollars) during the first eight months of 2025. Household loans increased by 711 billion yuan, while corporate and public institution loans grew by 22.12 trillion yuan. Total outstanding yuan loans reached 1.269 trillion yuan at the end of August, an 8.6 % year‑over‑year rise. The broad‑based money supply indicator 'M2' climbed 8.8 % to 98.331 trillion yuan, 'M1' rose 6 % to 23.111 trillion yuan, and the liquid cash indicator 'M0' increased 7.1 % to 13.34 trillion yuan. Deposits in yuan grew by 5.20 trillion yuan, with household deposits contributing 9.77 trillion yuan. Preliminary statistics show total financing for the real economy reached 56.26 trillion yuan, up 66.4 trillion yuan from the same period last year. The data were reported by the China News Agency (Xinhua) and cited by the central bank.

Key metrics: 
- Yuan loans: +46.13 trillion yuan (≈ 9.1 trillion USD)
- Household loans: +711 billion yuan
- Corporate/public loans: +22.12 trillion yuan
- Outstanding loans: 1.269 trillion yuan (↑ 8.6 %)
- M2: 98.331 trillion yuan (↑ 8.8 %)
- M1: 23.111 trillion yuan (↑ 6 %)
- M0: 13.34 trillion yuan (↑ 7.1 %)
- Deposits: 5.20 trillion yuan
- Real‑economy financing: 56.26 trillion yuan (↑ 66.4 trillion yuan)

The report highlights a significant expansion of credit and liquidity in China’s domestic financial system over the first eight months of the year.

title: Kredi kuruluşlarının nakdi kredileri 21 trilyonu aştı
content: As of August 2025, cash loans from credit institutions surpassed 21 trillion TL. The total amount of receivables to be written off reached 592 billion TL, with 566 billion TL owed to banks, 13 billion TL to financial leasing companies, 9 billion TL to factoring firms, and 5 billion TL to financing companies. The ratio of receivables to be written off to total loans increased to 2.7%, up 0.6 percentage points from the previous year. Commercial loans rose by 40% to 16.5 trillion TL, accounting for 76% of total loans. TL-denominated cash loans increased by 32% to 8.339 trillion TL, while foreign currency (YP) cash loans rose by 49% to 8.207 trillion TL, making up 50% of cash loans. Non-cash loans rose 45% year-on-year to 7.893 trillion TL. The manufacturing sector held the largest share among commercial loans at 31%, followed by wholesale and retail trade at over 19%. The construction sector had the highest write-off ratio at 4.5%, while the energy sector had the highest share of foreign currency cash loans at 85%. Individual loans exceeded 5.1 trillion TL, rising 48% year-on-year, with 99% provided by banks. Of the 23 billion TL in individual loans from financing companies, 11.9 billion TL were auto loans. Loan types were distributed as: 50% credit cards, 24% personal loans, 12% housing loans, 1% auto loans, and 13% loan-linked savings accounts. The write-off ratio for individual loans stood at 4%. The number of individual loan users (excluding those in collection) increased by 1.8 million to 42.8 million, with an average loan balance of 121,000 TL. In August, 224,000 people used a loan-linked savings account for the first time, 217,000 used a credit card for the first time, 111,000 took out a consumer loan, 14,000 used an auto loan, and 14,000 used a housing loan for the first time. Credit card limit utilization rate was 23%, with 41% of users having limits between 0–100,000 TL (accounting for 7% of total limit value). Total credit card limits amounted to 11.4 trillion TL, with 23% utilized. Istanbul led in individual loan share at 27%, followed by Ankara (10%) and İzmir (7%). Tunceli, Kahramanmaraş, and Adıyaman recorded the highest increases in individual loan balances over the past 12 months. Istanbul, Ankara, and İzmir had the highest per capita individual loan balances (including credit cards).

title: Personal loan interest rates in 2025 | Facts and statistics
content: The article explains how personal loan interest rates are affected by Federal Reserve policy and inflation. It notes that most personal loans are fixed‑rate, but variable‑rate borrowers are directly impacted by Fed rate hikes, while fixed‑rate borrowers feel the effect indirectly. Key metrics cited include an average personal loan interest rate of '12.57%', an average debt per borrower of '$10,749', and that Boomers hold the highest average balance of '20,370'. Inflation is reported at '2.5% month over month'. The Federal Reserve cut its interest rate for the first time in four years at its September meeting and cut it again in November, leaving the current federal funds target rate at '4.75% to 5%'. The piece warns that borrowers seeking new loans in 2024 will experience higher costs as rates rise. It also discusses how interest rates reflect market demand for credit and influence broader economic factors such as stocks, bonds, and consumer spending. Finally, it highlights that the pandemic caused a sharp drop in average rates, which have since rebounded and increased again.
